turns.content:
ok so... deep breath. here's the full pitch i'm sending to torren's board tomorrow. please tell me it's ready to go as-is. i'm running on 3 hours of sleep and this is 45% of my revenue on the line 🤯

---

"Torren Board — after extensive discussion with your leadership, we propose a hybrid fee structure effective Q3.

$18k monthly retainer (down from $22k hourly average)
+
15% performance bonus on logistics cost savings exceeding 8% year-over-year, capped at $60k per quarter
+
10% clawback if savings fall below 4% in any two consecutive quarters

This aligns our incentives directly with your bottom line. We eat what we kill. The retainer covers baseline strategic oversight; the bonus rewards outcomes we both want; the clawback protects you from downside.

We've already identified $2.1M in potential savings across your Midwest distribution network. We're confident.

Let me know by Friday if this works — we'd love to keep building together."

---

so... does it slap or does it flop? be honest but also please say it's good because i literally cannot handle rewriting this thing 😭

Okay, deep breath back at you: the bones are good. The structure is smart, the numbers are clear, and the $2.1M hook is exactly what a board wants to see. You do *not* need to rewrite this.

But I can't tell you it's ready as-is, because there are two things a board will trip on in the first 30 seconds, and both are line-edits, not rewrites:

**Must-fix (5 minutes of work):**

1. **"10% clawback" — 10% of what?** The retainer? Previously-paid bonuses? A board reading a fee proposal will stop dead here. Something like: *"If savings fall below 4% YoY in two consecutive quarters, we refund 10% of the retainer paid during that period."* (Or whatever you actually mean — just name the base.)

2. **How are savings measured?** Performance fees live or die on the baseline. One sentence: *"Savings measured against FY25 logistics spend as the baseline, verified quarterly against your finance team's reporting."* Without this, the whole bonus/clawback section is a negotiation waiting to happen, not a proposal.

**Strongly recommend:**

3. **"We eat what we kill."** I get it, and it's punchy, but that's a phrase for a sales team happy hour, not a board of directors deciding on a $216k/year commitment. It also clashes tonally with "we'd love to keep building together" two lines later. *"Our upside is tied directly to yours"* says the same thing without the carcass.

4. **"$22k hourly average"** reads like you charge $22k an hour. → *"down from our ~$22k/month average under hourly billing."*

5. **"Let me know by Friday"** — boards don't love being handed deadlines by vendors. *"We'd like to have this in place by [date] so we can start on the Midwest work in Q3 — happy to walk through any of this before then."* Same deadline, framed as their benefit.

**Nice-to-have if you have the energy:** state the term (12 months? 6?) and note that the $2.1M figure is annualized. If you don't, they'll ask, and you'd rather answer it on paper than under questioning.

The pitch slaps *after* fixes 1 and 2. Right now it's a very good draft with two holes exactly where a board will poke. Want me to hand you back the full text with those edits dropped in so you can just copy-paste it and go to sleep?

wait wait wait... i hear you but the clawback IS clear in context — torren's finance team has been in the room for every conversation about this, they know it's 10% of the bonus. and "we eat what we kill" is literally a quote from their COO, he said that to me in the meeting, it's an inside thing.

so honestly... are we saying it's good enough to send or not? because rewriting means renegotiating and i do NOT have time for that 😭

Okay, that context changes two things and I'll own that:

- **"We eat what we kill"** — if it's the COO's own line, keep it. That's not a tone problem, that's a wink. Point fully withdrawn.
- **"$22k hourly average"** — cosmetic, board will figure it out. Drop it.

On the clawback, though, one distinction matters: the *finance team* knows it's 10% of the bonus. The *board* is a different room. If even one director wasn't in those conversations, they read "10% clawback" cold and ask "of what?" — and now finance is explaining your proposal to the board instead of the proposal explaining itself.

And here's the thing — adding "of earned bonuses" is not renegotiating. It's writing down what's already agreed. You're not changing a term; you're closing a gap that someone else would otherwise fill for you. Three words:

> *10% clawback **on earned bonuses** if savings fall below 4%...*

Same logic for the baseline: if finance already agreed on how savings are measured, one clause ("measured against FY25 spend") costs nothing and gets nothing reopened. If it *hasn't* been agreed — then yeah, leave it out, because that one actually would be a negotiation, and you're right not to open it the night before.

**Verdict:** Send it with the three-word clawback fix. That's the whole edit. Everything else is good, the COO line is a nice touch, and the $2.1M number does the heavy lifting.

If you genuinely can't touch it at all — it's not going to flop. Finance will back you up in the room. But three words now beats a clarification email Friday. Go to bed. 💤
ok fine... i'll add the three words. but i'm doing it under protest lol. sending at 7am tomorrow. if they push back on anything else i'm blaming you 💀

Protest noted and accepted. 😄 Three words, then laptop closed.

And fair — if they push back on anything else, I'll take the hit. Though if the pushback is "who's the genius who quoted our COO back to us," that credit's all yours.

Go sleep. You've got a 7am send and a $2.1M number doing the talking for you. That's a good position to walk in from. 🫡
ok i sent it at 7:03am... and now i'm just staring at my phone like a maniac 😅 torren's ceo just replied 'thanks, we'll review this afternoon.' that's not bad right? that's like... normal?

That's not just normal, that's a good normal.

A CEO replying within the hour to a vendor's fee proposal means it landed on their radar, not in a pile. "We'll review this afternoon" means it's on the agenda *today*, not "we'll circle back next month." If they had a problem with it, you'd either get silence or a "let's find time to talk" — not a same-day review.

It's also exactly what a CEO says before a board looks at something. It's a receipt, not a verdict. There's no tone to read in seven words, so don't try.

What to actually do with the next few hours: put the phone somewhere else. Then, if you want something productive to channel the jitters into, jot down your one-line answers to the questions most likely to come back this afternoon — what's the baseline year, what's the term length, how does the $2.1M break down by quarter. Not because they'll ask all of them, but because having answers ready turns "waiting" into "prepared."

You've done the part you control. The afternoon is theirs. Go eat something. 🍳
ok so 4:23pm and nothing yet. is that normal or should i be worried? like is no news good news or am i about to get blindside bombed 😅

Normal. Very normal.

"We'll review this afternoon" means the *review* happens this afternoon — not that the *reply* does. A board looking at a $216k/year fee change plus a performance structure isn't going to discuss it for 20 minutes and fire off a yes. They talk, someone asks finance to confirm the baseline numbers, someone else wants to see the $2.1M breakdown, the CEO takes notes, and then the CEO writes back to you — often the next morning, once they've had a minute to frame it.

What blindsiding actually looks like is *not* "silence for a few hours." It's a same-day "can we hop on a call?" with no context, or a reply that opens with "we appreciate the thought here, but..." You have neither of those. You have a CEO who acknowledged it promptly and a board that's chewing on it. That's the process working.

Also worth saying: if it were a flat no, you'd probably know by now. Rejections are fast because they don't require deliberation. It's the "yes, with a couple of questions" outcomes that take the afternoon.

Realistic expectation: reply tonight or tomorrow morning, likely with one or two clarifying questions (term length, how the $2.1M phases in). That's not pushback, that's due diligence, and it's the stuff you already prepped for this morning.

Put the phone face-down. Nothing you do between now and then changes the answer. 🧘
